title: Game 2: Rubinstein–Capablanca
subtitle: A quiet king move makes the combination work

source.author: José Raúl Capablanca
source.section: Part II, Illustrative Games, Game 2: Queen’s Gambit Declined

steps.title: A setup aimed at the isolated pawn

narration.say: Rubinstein has White against Capablanca at San Sebastian in 1911. White’s development aims at Black’s isolated d-pawn.
White fianchettoes the bishop and castles. Black brings the rook out before completing development.
White exchanges on c5 and challenges the bishop with a knight.
White exchanges the knight for the bishop, then develops pressure against the centre.

steps.title: A tactical attack on the isolated pawn

narration.say: White exchanges on f6. Black recaptures with the queen.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Capture the central pawn with the knight.

steps.title: The move Capablanca had not considered

narration.say: Black’s queen attacks the bishop on h3. Instead of retreating the bishop, White can protect it with the king.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Protect the bishop with a quiet king move.

narration.say: White can now bring the queen to c1, attacking the bishop on c5.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Bring the queen to c1.

narration.say: White takes the bishop on c5. Black attacks with the queen, but White steers toward an ending.
White plays bishop to g4. Capablanca criticises this choice because it gives Black defensive chances.
Black brings the rook to d6. One pair of rooks is exchanged.
White takes the d-pawn, and the bishop and rook give checks.
Black plays a6. Capablanca criticises the loss of time.
White’s rook wins kingside pawns while Black advances on the other wing.
White gives checks and moves the bishop to d5. Black pushes b3.
Capablanca says Black missed a better defensive chance here. White captures on b3, and Black advances a3.
White takes the knight. Black recaptures the pawn, then advances a2.

steps.title: The rook reaches h6 with check

narration.say: White finishes with another rook check. Black resigns.
We end at the book’s final move. The preceding pawn race shows why a material advantage still requires care.

steps.title: Calculate quiet moves as well as forcing ones

narration.say: The central combination depended on king to g2: a quiet move that protected the bishop without abandoning the attack.
The ending was not flawless. Both players missed chances, and active defence made the conversion difficult.
A brilliant middle-game idea is only part of the job. You must still understand the ending it produces.
